question: Which of the following is NOT an approach for measuring unemployment in India?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Monthly Status Approach.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• India's official employment-unemployment surveys, conducted by the National Sample Survey Office (NSSO)/PLFS, measure unemployment using three standard approaches, not four. (बेरोजगारी मापन — मासिक स्थिति उपागम मौजूद नहीं)

 

• Usual Status Approach: Measures status based on the activity a person pursued for a majority of the 365 days preceding the survey (reference period of one year).

 

• Weekly Status Approach (Current Weekly Status): Measures status based on activity during a reference period of the preceding 7 days.

 

• Daily Status Approach (Current Daily Status): Measures status for each day of the preceding 7 days, recording each day separately, giving the most detailed picture of intermittent unemployment.

 

• There is no officially recognised "Monthly Status Approach" in Indian labour statistics methodology.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• These concepts were developed based on the recommendations of the Dantwala Committee (1970) on unemployment estimates.

 

• The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS), launched in 2017 by the NSSO, now provides employment-unemployment estimates on an annual and quarterly basis using these same reference periods.

 

NOTE

 

• Weekly Status Approach (Option 1): A genuine, officially used approach (7-day reference period) — incorrect choice for "NOT an approach".

 

• Daily Status Approach (Option 3): A genuine, officially used approach (day-wise reference within the week) — incorrect choice.

 

• Usual Status Approach (Option 4): A genuine, officially used approach (365-day reference period) — incorrect choice.

question: Saavaj is the official mascot of which of the following events?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 36th National Games of India.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Saavaj, a stylised lion, is the official mascot of the 36th National Games, hosted by Gujarat in 2022 (held between September-October 2022, with some events extending into early 2023). (साववज शुभंकर — 36वें राष्ट्रीय खेल)

 

• The mascot and anthem were unveiled by Union Home Minister Amit Shah in Ahmedabad, symbolising strength, agility and the Gujarati/Gir lion heritage of the state.

 

• The 36th National Games' motto was "Excellence Rises Here", and the events were held across multiple cities in Gujarat including Ahmedabad, Surat, Vadodara, Rajkot and Bhavnagar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Gir Forest National Park in Gujarat is the only home of the Asiatic lion in the wild, which inspired the Saavaj mascot design.

 

• The 37th National Games (2025) were held in Uttarakhand.

 

NOTE

 

• Khelo India Youth Games 2023 (Option 1): Held in Madhya Pradesh; its mascot was different (not Saavaj).

 

• FIH Men's World Cup Hockey 2023 (Option 2): Held in Odisha (Bhubaneswar-Rourkela); its mascot was "Olly" the Olive Ridley turtle.

 

• Commonwealth Games (Option 3): Not associated with the Saavaj mascot; the 2022 Birmingham Commonwealth Games' mascot was Perry the Bull.

question: In which of the following regions in India are there high-grade iron ore deposits?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Northern Odisha.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Northern Odisha, particularly the Barabil-Koira valley in Sundargarh, Keonjhar and Mayurbhanj districts, holds some of India's richest, high-grade haematite iron ore deposits. (उच्च श्रेणी लौह अयस्क — उत्तरी ओडिशा)

 

• Odisha is India's largest producer of iron ore, and this belt forms part of the extended Odisha-Jharkhand iron ore belt, which continues into Jharkhand's Singhbhum region.

 

• Major mining centres in this belt include Gua, Noamundi (Jharkhand) and Joda, Barbil, Koira (Odisha).

 

• Iron ore here is mainly haematite (Fe₂O₃), prized for its high iron content (60-70%), used extensively in steel plants like Rourkela Steel Plant.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's other major iron ore belts are the Bailadila range (Chhattisgarh), Bellary-Hospet (Karnataka) and Goa belt.

 

• Odisha also leads in chromite, bauxite and manganese production.

 

NOTE

 

• Western Rajasthan (Option 1): Known for copper (Khetri), gypsum, and salt (Sambhar Lake), not high-grade iron ore.

 

• Southern Punjab (Option 2): Punjab is largely an agricultural plain with negligible mineral deposits.

 

• Eastern Uttar Pradesh (Option 3): Known for limestone and some minor deposits, not a high-grade iron ore belt.

question: The deficiency of Vitamin A causes:
solution_text:
The correct answer is night blindness.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Vitamin A (Retinol) is essential for forming rhodopsin, the light-sensitive pigment in the retina's rod cells; its deficiency impairs vision in dim light, causing night blindness (nyctalopia). (विटामिन A की कमी — रतौंधी)

 

• Vitamin A is a fat-soluble vitamin, stored mainly in the liver, and obtained from sources like carrots, liver, eggs, and green leafy vegetables (as beta-carotene).

 

• Prolonged severe deficiency can also cause xerophthalmia (dryness of the cornea/conjunctiva), which can progress to keratomalacia and permanent blindness if untreated.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India runs the National Programme for Prevention of Blindness & Visual Impairment and periodic Vitamin A supplementation drives for children under the ICDS/NHM.

 

• Vitamin A was the first vitamin to be discovered, hence its designation as "A".

 

NOTE

 

• beriberi (Option 1): Caused by deficiency of Vitamin B1 (Thiamine).

 

• scurvy (Option 2): Caused by deficiency of Vitamin C (Ascorbic acid).

 

• rickets (Option 3): Caused by deficiency of Vitamin D (Calciferol), affecting bone mineralisation in children.

question: विजयनगर साम्राज्य के सबसे प्रसिद्ध शासक कृष्णदेव राय का संबंध किस राजवंश से था? (Krishnadeva Raya, the most famous ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, belonged to which dynasty?)
solution_text:
The correct answer is तुलुव / Tuluva.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Krishnadeva Raya (r. 1509-1529 CE), the most celebrated ruler of the Vijayanagara Empire, belonged to the Tuluva dynasty. (कृष्णदेव राय — तुलुव वंश)

 

• He was the third ruler of the Tuluva dynasty, succeeding Vira Narasimha, and is regarded as the greatest of all Vijayanagara rulers for his military conquests, administration and patronage of art and literature.

 

• His court housed the Ashtadiggajas, eight great Telugu poets, and he himself authored Amuktamalyada (Telugu) and Jambavati Kalyanam (Sanskrit).

 

• He defeated the Sultan of Bijapur, the Gajapati ruler of Odisha, and successfully repelled the Portuguese at various points, while maintaining friendly relations with the Portuguese for horse trade.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Krishnadeva Raya's guru and minister was Timmarusu (Appaji); the Hazara Rama Temple and Vitthala Temple at Hampi were built during his reign.

 

• The Vijayanagara Empire (1336-1646 CE) was ruled successively by four dynasties: Sangama, Saluva, Tuluva, and Aravidu.

 

NOTE

 

• अराविदु / Aravidu (Option 1): The last (4th) dynasty of Vijayanagara, founded by Tirumala Raya after the Battle of Talikota (1565).

 

• सुलुव / Saluva (Option 2): The 2nd dynasty, founded by Saluva Narasimha, who usurped the throne from the weakening Sangama dynasty.

 

• संगम / Sangama (Option 4): The founding (1st) dynasty of Vijayanagara, established by Harihara I and Bukka Raya I in 1336.

question: In 2022, what time did Chahat Arora wrap up the 100 m breaststroke race at the FINA World Swimming Championships in Melbourne, Australia?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1:13.13s.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian swimmer Chahat Arora clocked 1:13.13 seconds in the women's 100 m breaststroke at the 2022 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m), held at the Melbourne Sports and Aquatic Centre, Australia. (चाहत अरोड़ा — राष्ट्रीय रिकॉर्ड)

 

• This timing set a new National Record, breaking the previous mark, though she finished 42nd overall (3rd in her heat) and did not qualify for the semi-finals (only the top 16 advanced).

 

• The championship used a short-course (25 m) pool, distinct from the standard 50 m Olympic pool events.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The 2022 FINA World Swimming Championships (25 m) were held in December 2022 in Melbourne.

 

• FINA (Fédération Internationale de Natation) was later rebranded as World Aquatics in 2023.

 

NOTE

 

• 17:6.17s, 1:12.10s, 10:10.16s (Options 1, 3, 4): These are fabricated/incorrect timings not matching Chahat Arora's actual recorded national-record performance of 1:13.13s.

question: What is the full form of MEDP?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Micro Enterprise Development Programme.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• MEDP (Micro Enterprise Development Programme) is a skill-development and entrepreneurship-training initiative run under India's rural and urban livelihoods missions to help Self-Help Group (SHG) members set up and run micro-enterprises. (सूक्ष्म उद्यम विकास कार्यक्रम — MEDP)

 

• It is implemented as part of schemes like the National Rural Livelihoods Mission (NRLM/Ajeevika) and National Urban Livelihoods Mission (NULM), run by the Ministry of Rural Development / Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs.

 

• MEDP training covers business planning, financial literacy, market linkages and skill-building, enabling SHG members to become self-employed micro-entrepreneurs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• DAY-NRLM (Deendayal Antyodaya Yojana - National Rural Livelihoods Mission) promotes self-employment and organisation of rural poor into SHGs.

 

• MEDPs are often conducted in partnership with agencies like RSETI (Rural Self Employment Training Institutes).

 

NOTE

 

• Medium Enterprise Development Programme (Option 2): Incorrect expansion — MEDP targets micro, not medium, enterprises.

 

• Microfinance Entity Development Programme (Option 3): Not the correct/official expansion of the acronym.

 

• Micro Enterprise District Project (Option 4): Not the correct/official expansion; MEDP is a "Programme", not a "District Project".

question: Bhimsen Joshi belongs to which of the following classical music traditions?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Kirana Gharana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Pandit Bhimsen Joshi (1922-2011), the legendary Hindustani classical vocalist, belonged to the Kirana Gharana. (भीमसेन जोशी — किराना घराना)

 

• He was a disciple of Sawai Gandharva (Rambhau Kundgolkar), himself a prominent exponent of the Kirana Gharana founded by Ustad Abdul Karim Khan.

 

• Bhimsen Joshi was renowned for his mastery of khayal singing and received the Bharat Ratna in 2008 and Padma Vibhushan in 1999.

 

• He founded the "Sawai Gandharva Bhimsen Mahotsav", an annual classical music festival held in Pune in memory of his guru.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Kirana Gharana is known for its emphasis on raga elaboration (bandish) and note-bending (meend); other notable Kirana exponents include Gangubai Hangal and Prabha Atre.

 

• Bhimsen Joshi also sang in the famous devotional collaboration "Mile Sur Mera Tumhara".

 

NOTE

 

• Delhi Gharana (Option 1): Associated with vocalists like Ustad Chand Khan; one of the oldest khayal gharanas.

 

• Banaras Gharana (Option 2): Known primarily for thumri, tabla and Kathak; associated with artists like Girija Devi.

 

• Jaipur Gharana (Option 4): Known for Jaipur-Atrauli khayal style, founded by Ustad Alladiya Khan; exponents include Kishori Amonkar.

question:
While travelling in a train, one of the travellers started speaking against the Indian freedom struggle and noble ideals of it.

Which of the following Articles mentions the fundamental duties in relation to such circumstances?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Article 51A (b).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 51A, added by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976 on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee, lists the Fundamental Duties of Indian citizens. (मौलिक कर्तव्य — अनुच्छेद 51A)

 

• Article 51A(b) specifically enjoins every citizen "to cherish and follow the noble ideals which inspired our national struggle for freedom" — directly matching the scenario of someone disparaging the freedom struggle and its ideals.

 

• Originally 10 fundamental duties were listed; an 11th duty (regarding parents providing education to children aged 6-14) was added by the 86th Amendment Act, 2002.

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR and, like the DPSPs, are non-justiciable (not enforceable by courts).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 51A(a) requires citizens "to abide by the Constitution and respect its ideals and institutions, the National Flag and the National Anthem".

 

• Fundamental Duties are placed in Part IV-A of the Constitution, immediately after the Directive Principles of State Policy (Part IV).

 

NOTE

 

• Article 51A(c) (Option 2): Duty "to uphold and protect the sovereignty, unity and integrity of India" — not specific to freedom-struggle ideals.

 

• Article 51A(a) (Option 3): Duty regarding the Constitution, National Flag and National Anthem — not about the freedom struggle specifically.

 

• Article 51A(d) (Option 4): Duty "to defend the country and render national service when called upon to do so" — unrelated to this scenario.

question:
In India, credit creation is done by:

A) Ministry of Finance

B) Reserve Bank of India

C) Commercial Banks
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only C.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Credit creation in India is the function of Commercial Banks, which lend out a portion of deposits (keeping a fraction as reserves, i.e., the CRR), thereby multiplying the money supply through the credit multiplier/money multiplier process. (साख सृजन — वाणिज्यिक बैंक)

 

• When a bank grants a loan, it credits the borrower's account, and this deposit again becomes available for further lending, repeating the cycle and "creating" credit far in excess of the original deposit base.

 

• The Reserve Bank of India (RBI) *regulates* the money supply and credit creation (via CRR, SLR, repo rate, etc.) but does not itself create credit through commercial lending to the public — it is the monetary authority/central bank, not a credit-creating retail institution.

 

• The Ministry of Finance frames fiscal policy and manages government finances; it has no direct role in credit creation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The extent of credit creation depends on the Cash Reserve Ratio (CRR) — a lower CRR allows banks to create more credit.

 

• RBI's tools like Repo Rate, Reverse Repo, CRR and SLR are used to control (not directly perform) the credit creation done by commercial banks.

 

NOTE

 

• Only B (Option 2): Incorrect — RBI regulates/controls credit creation but does not itself create credit through public lending.

 

• All – A, B and C (Option 3): Incorrect — neither the Ministry of Finance nor RBI directly creates credit.

 

• Only A (Option 4): Incorrect — the Ministry of Finance has no role in credit creation.

question: Who among the following devoted his life for the upliftment of widows and established the Widow Remarriage Association in 1893?
solution_text:
The correct answer is DK Karve.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Dhondo Keshav Karve (D.K. Karve / Maharshi Karve) devoted his life to the welfare of Hindu widows and founded the Widow Remarriage Association in 1893. (धोंडो केशव कर्वे — विधवा पुनर्विवाह संघ, 1893)

 

• He himself controversially married a widow, Godubai, in 1893, defying orthodox social norms of the time, and went on to found the Hindu Widows' Home Association in Pune (1896).

 

• In 1916, he established SNDT Women's University, India's first women's university, named after his benefactor Sir Vithaldas Thackersey.

 

• He was honoured with the Bharat Ratna in 1958 for his contributions to women's education and social reform.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Karve was influenced by the earlier widow-remarriage reform work of Ishwar Chandra Vidyasagar in Bengal.

 

• Karve lived to 104 years, one of the longest-lived major social reformers of modern India.

 

NOTE

 

• Annie Besant (Option 2): Theosophist and Home Rule Movement leader; founded the Central Hindu College, Banaras — not associated with the 1893 Widow Remarriage Association.

 

• KC Sen (Option 3): Keshab Chandra Sen led the Brahmo Samaj (Brahmo Samaj of India) and campaigned against child marriage via the Native Marriage Act, 1872 — not this specific association.

 

• BM Malabari (Option 4): Behramji Malabari campaigned against child marriage and enforced widowhood, notably influencing the Age of Consent Act, 1891, but did not found the 1893 Widow Remarriage Association.

question: In diffraction of white light by a prism, which colour of light from VIBGYOR will be bent most?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Violet.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• When white light passes through a prism, it splits into its constituent colours (VIBGYOR) — a phenomenon called dispersion. (प्रकाश का विक्षेपण — बैंगनी रंग सबसे अधिक मुड़ता है)

 

• The extent of bending (refraction) of each colour depends on its wavelength: shorter wavelengths bend more, longer wavelengths bend less.

 

• Violet light has the shortest wavelength (~380-450 nm) among VIBGYOR and hence the highest refractive index, causing it to bend the most.

 

• Red light has the longest wavelength (~620-750 nm) and the lowest refractive index, so it bends the least.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The VIBGYOR sequence (Violet, Indigo, Blue, Green, Yellow, Orange, Red) represents decreasing wavelength to increasing wavelength, i.e., decreasing to increasing bending order is reversed — violet bends most, red bends least.

 

• This same principle explains the formation of a rainbow, where water droplets act as tiny prisms.

 

NOTE

 

• Red (Option 1): Bends the least, not the most, due to its longest wavelength.

 

• Yellow (Option 2): Bends less than violet; it lies in the middle of the visible spectrum.

 

• Green (Option 3): Bends less than violet and indigo/blue; also lies in the middle of the spectrum.

question:
Match list I with list II and choose your answer from the code below.

List-I: (a) Habeas corpus (b) Mandamus (c) Quo warranto (d) Certiorari

List-II: (i) Enquiring into legality of claim (ii) To command (iii) To have a body of (iv) To be certified
solution_text:
The correct answer is a-iii, b-ii, c-i, d-iv.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• These pairings are based on the literal Latin meanings of the five writs enumerated under Articles 32 and 226 of the Indian Constitution. (रिट के लैटिन अर्थ — बंदी प्रत्यक्षीकरण)

 

• Habeas Corpus literally means "to have a body of" — it directs that a detained person be physically produced before the court to examine the legality of detention. (a-iii)

 

• Mandamus literally means "to command" — issued to a public authority to perform a duty it has failed/refused to perform. (b-ii)

 

• Quo Warranto literally means "by what authority/warrant" — used to enquire into the legality of a claim made by a person to hold a public office. (c-i)

 

• Certiorari literally means "to be certified" or "to be informed" — issued by a higher court to quash an order of a lower court/tribunal that has exceeded its jurisdiction. (d-iv)

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The fifth writ, Prohibition, means "to forbid" and is issued to prevent a lower court/tribunal from exceeding its jurisdiction.

 

• Article 32 (right to constitutional remedies) allows the Supreme Court to issue writs; Article 226 allows High Courts to issue writs — the latter's writ jurisdiction is broader (for any legal right, not just fundamental rights).

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 mismatch the writs with incorrect Latin meanings — none corresponds correctly to all four writs' literal etymology.

question: Name the campaign launched by the Madhya Pradesh government on the occasion of National Girl Child Day on January 24, 2021, under the 'Beti Bachao Beti Padhao' scheme.
solution_text:
The correct answer is PANKH Abhiyan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Madhya Pradesh government, under then Chief Minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan, launched the "PANKH Abhiyan" on National Girl Child Day, 24 January 2021, as part of the Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme. (पंख अभियान — बालिका सशक्तिकरण, मध्य प्रदेश)

 

• PANKH stands for empowering the girl child, aiming to build a positive environment for girls' growth, education, health and safety, and change societal attitudes towards the girl child.

 

• It was launched alongside the 13th National Girl Child Day, and included initiatives spanning awareness campaigns, community engagement and convergence with health/education departments.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• National Girl Child Day is observed every year on 24 January in India, since 2008, to raise awareness about the inequalities faced by girls.

 

• The nationwide Beti Bachao Beti Padhao scheme was launched by the Government of India in January 2015 at Panipat, Haryana, to address the declining Child Sex Ratio.

 

NOTE

 

• Mazi Kanya Bhagyashree Scheme (Option 1): A girl-child welfare scheme of the Maharashtra government, not Madhya Pradesh.

 

• CBSE Udaan scheme (Option 2): A CBSE initiative to promote girls' enrolment in engineering colleges, unrelated to the MP government's National Girl Child Day campaign.

 

• Balika Samridhi Yojana (Option 3): A central government scheme (launched 1997) providing scholarships/grants to girl children below the poverty line, not this MP state campaign.

question: Lotia is a regional music form of which state?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Rajasthan.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Lotia (also spelt Lotiya) is a traditional folk-music form of Rajasthan, sung predominantly during festive and social occasions. (लोटिया लोकगीत — राजस्थान)

 

• Rajasthani folk music is renowned for its rich variety, including forms like Maand, Panihari, Kurjan and Lotia, traditionally performed by communities such as the Manganiyars and Langas.

 

• Rajasthan's arid landscape and distinct cultural traditions have given rise to a wide range of region-specific folk songs tied to seasons, festivals, and daily life (e.g., water-fetching, monsoon songs).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Maand is considered the classical folk-music form of Rajasthan, often associated with royal courts.

 

• Rajasthan's famous folk dances include Ghoomar, Kalbelia and Chari.

 

NOTE

 

• Odisha (Option 1): Known for folk forms like Pala and Daskathia, not Lotia.

 

• Assam (Option 3): Known for Bihu songs and Ojapali, not Lotia.

 

• Bihar (Option 4): Known for folk forms like Chaita and Sohar, not Lotia.

question:
Which of the following statements is/are FALSE with respect to simple model of circular flow of economy?

i. The aggregate consumption is more than aggregate expenditure.

ii. There is government intervention.

iii. There are no trade activities with the rest of the world.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only i.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The simple (closed, domestic) model of the circular flow of income, as used in national income accounting, includes households, firms and the government sector, but excludes the foreign/external sector. (वृत्तीय प्रवाह मॉडल — कथन i असत्य)

 

• In this domestic circular-flow model, aggregate expenditure = consumption expenditure (C) + investment expenditure (I) + government expenditure (G) — since expenditure includes additional components beyond consumption alone, aggregate consumption cannot be "more than" aggregate expenditure. Statement i is FALSE.

 

• Statement ii is TRUE: The government sector is very much a part of this "simple"/domestic model — the government collects taxes and spends on goods/services/transfers, forming a key leakage-injection pair in the flow.

 

• Statement iii is TRUE: By definition, the "simple"/domestic model of the circular flow excludes foreign trade (exports and imports) — it is treated as a closed economy with respect to the rest of the world, which is only introduced in the four-sector (open economy) model.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The four-sector (open economy) circular flow model adds the foreign sector, incorporating exports and imports as additional injections/leakages.

 

• Leakages from the circular flow include savings, taxes and imports; injections include investment, government spending and exports.

 

NOTE

 

• Only i and iii (Option 1): Incorrect — statement iii is a true, not false, description of the simple/domestic model (it correctly excludes foreign trade).

 

• Only iii (Option 3): Incorrect — statement iii is true, and this option misses statement i, which is actually false.

 

• Only ii and iii (Option 4): Incorrect — statement ii is a true description (government is part of this model), and statement iii is also true; neither is false.

question: Which of the following Indian classical dancers was the recipient of the Padma Vibhushan award of 2003?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sonal Mansingh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Sonal Mansingh, a celebrated exponent of Bharatanatyam and Odissi, was conferred the Padma Vibhushan in 2003. (सोनल मानसिंह — पद्म विभूषण, 2003)

 

• She had earlier received the Padma Bhushan in 1992 and was later nominated as a member of the Rajya Sabha (2018-2024).

 

• She is the founder of the Centre for Indian Classical Dances (CID) in Delhi and is a recipient of the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award as well.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Padma Vibhushan is India's second-highest civilian award, after the Bharat Ratna.

 

• Sonal Mansingh has been an active advocate for causes including women's empowerment and environmental conservation through her art.

 

NOTE

 

• Saswati Sen (Option 1): A noted Kathak dancer and disciple of Birju Maharaj; received the Padma Shri, not Padma Vibhushan 2003.

 

• Elam Endira Devi (Option 2): A Manipuri dance exponent; not the 2003 Padma Vibhushan recipient in this category.

 

• Birju Maharaj (Option 3): The legendary Kathak maestro received the Padma Vibhushan in 1986, not 2003.

question: The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI) does NOT include which of the following indicators?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gender development index.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI), developed by economist Morris David Morris in the 1970s, is a composite measure combining exactly three indicators. (भौतिक जीवन गुणवत्ता सूचकांक — तीन संकेतक)

 

• The three PQLI indicators are: (1) Infant Mortality Rate, (2) Life Expectancy at age one, and (3) Basic Literacy Rate.

 

• PQLI was among the early attempts (before the UNDP's Human Development Index, HDI, introduced in 1990) to measure well-being beyond mere per-capita income.

 

• The Gender Development Index (GDI), in contrast, is a separate, later index (introduced by UNDP) measuring gender-based disparities in HDI's core dimensions (health, education, income) — it is not part of PQLI.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• PQLI scores each indicator on a 0-100 scale and averages them to give the composite index.

 

• The UNDP's HDI (Human Development Index) uses life expectancy, education (mean/expected years of schooling) and GNI per capita.

 

NOTE

 

• Life expectancy (Option 1): One of the three genuine PQLI components — incorrect choice.

 

• Infant mortality (Option 3): One of the three genuine PQLI components — incorrect choice.

 

• Literacy (Option 4): One of the three genuine PQLI components — incorrect choice.

question: Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra is the cultural festival of which of the following Indian states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Assam.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Rajini Gabra and Harni Gabra are important socio-religious festivals of the Dimasa tribe of Assam. (राजिनी गबरा और हरनी गबरा — असम की डिमासा जनजाति)

 

• These festivals are celebrated as introductory/preparatory festivals before the sowing/cultivation season, involving propitiation of family deities.

 

• Rajini Gabra is celebrated during the daytime, led by the village headman known as the "Kunang", while Harni Gabra is its associated nocturnal counterpart.

 

• The Dimasa are one of the major indigenous tribal communities of Assam, concentrated in districts like Dima Hasao (North Cachar Hills) and Cachar.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable festivals of the Dimasa community include Busu Dima, a major post-harvest festival.

 

• Assam's other well-known festivals include Bihu (celebrated thrice a year, marking agricultural/seasonal cycles).

 

NOTE

 

• Bihar (Option 2): Known for festivals like Chhath Puja and Sonepur Mela, not Rajini/Harni Gabra.

 

• Mizoram (Option 3): Known for festivals like Chapchar Kut, not Rajini/Harni Gabra.

 

• West Bengal (Option 4): Known for festivals like Durga Puja and Poila Boishakh, not Rajini/Harni Gabra.

question: Who was appointed as the first woman Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU), New Delhi?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Santishree Pandit.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Santishree Dhulipudi Pandit was appointed as the first woman Vice-Chancellor of Jawaharlal Nehru University (JNU) in February 2022. (शांतिश्री पंडित — पहली महिला कुलपति, JNU)

 

• She is a political scientist specialising in international relations, and prior to JNU, she served as Pro-Vice-Chancellor of the University of Mumbai and Vice-Chancellor of Savitribai Phule Pune University (SPPU).

 

• JNU was established in 1969, and Santishree Pandit's appointment marked the first time a woman headed the university in its history.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• JNU is known for its strong programmes in social sciences, international relations, and languages, and is located in New Delhi.

 

• Santishree Pandit is the daughter of noted linguist Prof. G.N. Devy's contemporaries in academia; she is a specialist on South Asian and international politics.

 

NOTE

 

• Geeta Bhat (Option 1): Not associated with the JNU Vice-Chancellorship.

 

• Jayati Ghosh (Option 2): A well-known economist and former JNU professor, but never JNU Vice-Chancellor.

 

• Utsa Patnaik (Option 3): A renowned Marxist economist and former JNU professor, but never JNU Vice-Chancellor.

question: What numerical scale was introduced in 1932 that determined the electronegativity of fluorine to be 4.0?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pauling scale.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pauling scale, proposed by the American chemist Linus Pauling in 1932, is the most widely used scale for measuring electronegativity of elements. (पॉलिंग पैमाना — इलेक्ट्रोनगेटिविटी)

 

• On this scale, Fluorine (the most electronegative element) is assigned a value of 4.0, the highest on the scale, against which all other elements are compared.

 

• The scale is based on bond dissociation energies, using the difference between the actual bond energy of a heteronuclear bond and the expected (geometric mean) value from homonuclear bonds.

 

• Linus Pauling is also famous for winning two unshared Nobel Prizes — the Nobel Prize in Chemistry (1954) and the Nobel Peace Prize (1962).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The general trend of electronegativity is that it increases across a period (left to right) and decreases down a group in the periodic table.

 

• Caesium/Francium are generally considered among the least electronegative elements.

 

NOTE

 

• Allred-Rochow scale (Option 1): A later (1958) electronegativity scale based on the effective nuclear charge experienced by valence electrons — not the 1932 scale with F = 4.0.

 

• Mulliken scale (Option 2): Based on the average of ionisation energy and electron affinity, proposed by Robert Mulliken — a different scale, not the 1932 Pauling scale.

 

• Jae scale (Option 4): Not a recognised standard electronegativity scale.

question: Which of these is NOT one of the impacts of the green revolution?
option_1: A loosening of traditional bonds or hereditary relationships between farmers or landowners and agricultural workers.
option_2: The rise of a class of 'free' wage labourers.
option_3: A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain).
option_4: There was an increase in the use of agricultural labour as cultivation became more intensive.
solution_text:
The correct answer is A shift from payment in cash to payment in kind (grain).

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Green Revolution (from the mid-1960s), which introduced HYV seeds, chemical fertilisers and irrigation, brought major socio-economic changes in Indian agrarian relations. (हरित क्रांति — नकद भुगतान की ओर बदलाव)

 

• As agriculture became commercialised, there was actually a documented shift from payment in KIND (grain) to payment in CASH for agricultural wage labour — the reverse of what this option states.

 

• The Green Revolution genuinely caused: loosening of traditional patron-client bonds between landowners and workers, the emergence of "free" wage labourers (no longer tied by traditional obligations), and an increase in the demand for agricultural labour due to more intensive multiple cropping.

 

• Because this option reverses the actual direction of the cash-kind shift, it correctly identifies the statement that is NOT a genuine impact of the Green Revolution.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Green Revolution was pioneered in India largely due to the efforts of agricultural scientist M.S. Swaminathan, aided by Norman Borlaug's high-yielding wheat varieties.

 

• It was most successful in states like Punjab, Haryana and Western Uttar Pradesh.

 

NOTE

 

• Loosening of traditional bonds (Option 1): A genuine, well-documented social impact of the Green Revolution — incorrect choice for "NOT an impact".

 

• Rise of 'free' wage labourers (Option 2): A genuine impact, as commercialisation reduced traditional bonded/attached labour relationships — incorrect choice.

 

• Increase in agricultural labour use (Option 4): A genuine impact, as intensive multiple cropping increased demand for labour — incorrect choice.

question: Which of the following steps is NOT involved in a Water Cycle?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Hydration.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Water Cycle (Hydrological Cycle) describes the continuous movement of water on, above and below the Earth's surface, involving the key processes of Evaporation, Condensation, Precipitation, along with Transpiration, Infiltration, Runoff and Collection. (जल चक्र — वाष्पीकरण, संघनन, वर्षण)

 

• Evaporation: Water from oceans, rivers and lakes turns into water vapour due to heat from the sun.

 

• Condensation: Water vapour rises, cools, and condenses into tiny droplets, forming clouds.

 

• Precipitation: When droplets in clouds combine and become heavy enough, they fall back to Earth as rain, snow, sleet or hail.

 

• "Hydration" is a chemistry/biology term (referring to the addition of water to a substance, or maintaining bodily water levels) and is not a recognised stage of the water cycle.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other recognised water-cycle processes include Transpiration (water release from plants), Infiltration (water seeping into soil) and Runoff (surface flow of water into water bodies).

 

• The water cycle is powered primarily by solar energy and gravity.

 

NOTE

 

• Condensation (Option 2): A genuine, core step of the water cycle — incorrect choice.

 

• Precipitation (Option 3): A genuine, core step of the water cycle — incorrect choice.

 

• Evaporation (Option 4): A genuine, core step of the water cycle — incorrect choice.

question: In which year did Rudrankksh Patil win gold in men's 10 m air rifle event in ISSF World Cup?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 2023.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Indian shooter Rudrankksh Balasaheb Patil won the gold medal in the men's 10 m air rifle event at the ISSF World Cup 2023, held in Cairo, Egypt. (रुद्रांक्ष पाटिल — ISSF विश्व कप 2023, स्वर्ण पदक)

 

• He became a world champion, setting a new benchmark for Indian rifle shooting on the global stage, and has since won further medals at subsequent ISSF World Cups (including 2025 editions).

 

• Rudrankksh Patil is known for his composure and technical precision in 10 m air rifle shooting, representing India in major international shooting events.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The ISSF (International Shooting Sport Federation) organises the annual ISSF World Cup series across multiple shooting disciplines (rifle, pistol, shotgun).

 

• India has emerged as a strong shooting nation in recent years, with shooters like Manu Bhaker, Sift Kaur Samra and Rudrankksh Patil winning global medals.

 

NOTE

 

• 2022, 2020, 2021 (Options 1, 2, 4): Incorrect years — Rudrankksh Patil's ISSF World Cup gold in the men's 10 m air rifle event came in 2023, not these years.

question: Which of the following is true about the Indian Desert?
option_1: Bounded to the west by the Aravalli
option_2: Lies to the southeast of the Aravali
option_3: Lies to the northwest of the Aravali
option_4: Bounded to the south by the Aravali
solution_text:
The correct answer is Lies to the northwest of the Aravali.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Indian Desert (Thar Desert / Marusthali) lies to the northwest of the Aravalli Range, extending across western Rajasthan into parts of Gujarat, Haryana and Punjab, up to the Indo-Pakistan border. (भारतीय मरुस्थल — अरावली के उत्तर-पश्चिम में)

 

• The Aravalli Range acts as a watershed and climatic barrier, blocking the southwest monsoon winds from reaching the desert region, contributing to its aridity.

 

• The Thar Desert has undulating topography, with sand dunes called 'Dhrian', and is characterised by low, irregular rainfall (mostly below 150 mm/year in the western parts).

 

• The Luni River is the only significant river in this region, which drains into the Rann of Kachchh.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Aravalli Range is one of the oldest fold mountain ranges in the world, running roughly from Gujarat through Rajasthan (Delhi Ridge) up to Delhi.

 

• Mount Abu (Guru Shikhar), the highest peak of the Aravallis (1,722 m), is located in this region.

 

NOTE

 

• Bounded to the west by the Aravalli (Option 1): Incorrect direction — the desert lies to the northwest, not merely bounded to the west.

 

• Lies to the southeast of the Aravali (Option 2): Incorrect direction — this is the opposite (the fertile plains, not the desert, generally lie southeast/east of the Aravallis).

 

• Bounded to the south by the Aravali (Option 4): Incorrect — the desert's relation to the Aravallis is northwest, not a southern boundary.
